principles: Prefer one obvious default path for ordinary developers.
Preserve existing automation as compatibility aliases unless a real correctness issue forces a break.
Do not add multi-tenant or broader auth redesign work to a filename/bundle story.
Keep the implementation aligned with the docs and the visible developer experience.
drivers: Ordinary developers should get a simple bundle without extra fields.
Senior bundle creation must be explicit opt-in.
Legacy authority_trust.env and staging-client.env paths must remain usable.

options.name: new-names-default-with-aliases
pros: Matches the requested Lattice-prefixed naming while keeping current automation working.
Keeps the default developer workflow simple.
Lets the senior variant stay explicit rather than implicit.
cons: Needs alias handling and extra docs/tests.
Requires careful verification that both file-name families stay in sync.

options.name: keep-legacy-names-only
pros: Avoids touching existing file generation paths.
cons: Does not satisfy the naming cleanup request.
Leaves the developer-facing vocabulary inconsistent with the Lattice naming scheme.

options.name: replace-legacy-names-entirely
pros: Cleanest end state from a naming perspective.
cons: Breaks existing automation and source compatibility.
Raises rollout risk for a story that is supposed to simplify access, not destabilize it.

rationale: It satisfies the new Lattice naming request, keeps the default path simple, and preserves legacy compatibility so we do not break current users while cleaning up the bundle flow.

preMortem.scenario: Legacy scripts fail after the rename
preMortem.trigger: The generator writes only the new names or the alias mapping is incomplete.
preMortem.consequence: Existing automation cannot source the expected files.
preMortem.mitigation: Write both name families from the same source and add coverage for both paths.

preMortem.scenario: The senior path becomes the default by accident
preMortem.trigger: The opt-in flag is ignored or defaults are wired backwards.
preMortem.consequence: Ordinary developers face extra complexity and the bundle story stops being simple.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep the default bundle path explicitly separate and test the default vs senior outputs independently.

preMortem.scenario: Docs drift away from the actual bundle behavior
preMortem.trigger: Implementation changes land without updating the developer-facing bundle guidance.
preMortem.consequence: People cannot tell which filenames to use and support overhead rises.
preMortem.mitigation: Update the authority docs in the same story and verify the filenames in examples.

preMortem.scenario: Secret values leak in logs or generated text
preMortem.trigger: Debug output prints raw keys or trust material.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep the generator file-only, redact values in logs, and avoid printing secret contents.
